key_insight: Specialized, physics-aware machine learning force fields are needed to reliably simulate complex materials dynamics where general-purpose MLIPs break down under reactive, non-equilibrium, and large-scale fracture conditions.
engineering_relevance: For solid mechanics and fracture simulations, task-specific ML force fields can extend atomistic accuracy to the length and time scales relevant to damage evolution, but only if they are validated against the target observables.
method: Assess MLIP design trade-offs: strained-state coverage, message-passing cost, and nonlocal interactions
Benchmark specialized potentials across four hard scenarios: electrified interfaces, open systems, multiphase evolution, and fracture
Use observable-specific validation rather than relying only on near-equilibrium zero-shot performance
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes evidence across four demanding application contexts to compare model behavior against intended observables, highlighting where pretrained equivariant GNNs succeed or fail.
watch_item: High-order architectures and extrapolation to highly strained or reactive states can be computationally expensive and unreliable without careful, application-specific training and validation.
paper_title: Specialized machine learning force fields for materials dynamics
